doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Modern Touch session with Max Roach, billed as Spider Maxwell
summary: Brown goes through albums from 1957; Golson recalls his Riverside date with Max Roach, who agreed to record with an unknown leader.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You finished up in the chronology with Art Blakey. Before we get into the Jazztet, which is obviously a watershed in your career, I want to go back and look at some of the recordings that you made after you got – from ’57 up until the Jazztet. You had several – you’re quite prolific.
That’s when I started to really record.

Right. I’ve got a few titles here of albums that might jog your memory. Here’s one called The Modern Touch. Benny Golson sextet, right? Jay Jay Johnson, Kenny Dorham, Wynton Kelly, Paul Chambers, and on drums, Max Roach.
Max Roach, who was called Spider Maxwell, I think, on this, because he had a contract with some other company
This one’s on Riverside, produced by Orrin Keepnews. Any other recollections about this particular – I’m going to go through several . . .

Oh, I remember it all. The thing I remember about it most – I was the only one on there not known, and it was my date. I asked Max Roach, years later, why would you agree to record with this no-name guy? He said, “Oh, I heard about you.”
